items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: and I think Freddie Webster -- have you ever heard of Freddy Webster? He was quite a trumpet player. He was working with Erskine Tate at that time. And I stayed in Chicago and I left and after -- my mother died, I left -- I stayed there a little while, then I left and

ctx.x: And then I went back to Chicago, because my mother

was very ill. And I just stayed and worked around there. And the band -- let's see, the band around Chicago at that time was Erskine Tate, and he had all of the fine musicians, and I think Freddie Webster -- have you ever heard of Freddy Webster? He was quite a trumpet player. He was working with Erskine Tate at that time. And I stayed in Chicago and I left and after -- my mother died, I left -- I stayed there a little while, then I left and joined Roy again in New York.
And I worke-d at the -- I forget the name of this ballroom -- the Arcade Ballroom in New York, opposite Les Brown. He was the other band. It was -- what kind of -- almost like a taxi dance, you know.
